lessons.description: Expand your verb knowledge beyond the present tense. Learn the past (Imperfect) and future tenses to describe actions across time.

quiz.question: Which tense is “Present (वर्तमान)”?

quiz.answer: Used for actions happening now or generally true.

quiz.question: Which tense is “Future (लृट्)”?
options: Used for actions that will happen.
Used for simple past actions (narrative past).

lessons.title: Participles – Part 1 (कृत् प्रत्यय)
lessons.description: Learn the essential participle forms: Past Passive Participle (क्त), Future Passive Participle (तव्य/अनीयर्), and Gerund (क्त्वा). These are crucial for expressing completed actions, obligations, and sequential actions.

quiz.question: Which participle type is “Past Passive Participle (क्त)”?
options: Indicates an action completed before another action. Translates as 'having done...'.
Indicates a completed action. The most common participle in Sanskrit. Usually translates as 'having been...' or simply as a past passive adjective.
Indicates obligation, necessity, or possibility. Translates as 'must be...', 'should be...', 'fit to be...'.
quiz.answer: Indicates a completed action. The most common participle in Sanskrit. Usually translates as 'having been...' or simply as a past passive adjective.

quiz.question: Which participle type is “Future Passive Participle (तव्य / अनीयर्)”?
options: Indicates an action completed before another action. Translates as 'having done...'.
Indicates obligation, necessity, or possibility. Translates as 'must be...', 'should be...', 'fit to be...'.
Indicates a completed action. The most common participle in Sanskrit. Usually translates as 'having been...' or simply as a past passive adjective.
quiz.answer: Indicates obligation, necessity, or possibility. Translates as 'must be...', 'should be...', 'fit to be...'.

quiz.question: How is the Past Passive Participle (क्त) formed?
options: Root + (इ)त or (आ)न; often takes a prefix
Root + त्वा (or या for compound verbs)
quiz.answer: Root + (इ)त or (आ)न; often takes a prefix

quiz.question: How is the Gerund (क्त्वा) formed?
options: Root + (इ)त or (आ)न; often takes a prefix
Root + त्वा (or या for compound verbs)
quiz.answer: Root + त्वा (or या for compound verbs)

lessons.title: Participles – Part 2 (Advanced)
lessons.description: Master the remaining participle forms: Present active participle (शतृ/शानच्), Future active participle, and conditional forms for advanced reading.

quiz.question: Which participle type is “Present Active Participle (शतृ)”?
options: Middle voice present participle, often used for reflexive or intransitive verbs.
Indicates an action that will happen; translates as 'about to ...' or 'going to ...'.
Expresses a hypothetical action; uses the conditional mood.
Indicates an action that is ongoing; translates as '...ing'.
quiz.answer: Indicates an action that is ongoing; translates as '...ing'.

quiz.question: Which participle type is “Present Active Participle (शानच्)”?
options: Expresses a hypothetical action; uses the conditional mood.
Indicates an action that will happen; translates as 'about to ...' or 'going to ...'.
Middle voice present participle, often used for reflexive or intransitive verbs.
Indicates an action that is ongoing; translates as '...ing'.
quiz.answer: Middle voice present participle, often used for reflexive or intransitive verbs.

quiz.question: Which participle type is “Future Active Participle”?
options: Indicates an action that will happen; translates as 'about to ...' or 'going to ...'.
Middle voice present participle, often used for reflexive or intransitive verbs.
Expresses a hypothetical action; uses the conditional mood.
Indicates an action that is ongoing; translates as '...ing'.
quiz.answer: Indicates an action that will happen; translates as 'about to ...' or 'going to ...'.

quiz.question: Which participle type is “Conditional”?
options: Expresses a hypothetical action; uses the conditional mood.
Middle voice present participle, often used for reflexive or intransitive verbs.
Indicates an action that is ongoing; translates as '...ing'.
Indicates an action that will happen; translates as 'about to ...' or 'going to ...'.
quiz.answer: Expresses a hypothetical action; uses the conditional mood.
